title: The Grace of Giving
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro

outline.title: Testimony in the Context of Generosity
subpoints: Paul’s repetition of the appeal is superfluous but necessary for importance
The Corinthians’ promise to the Jerusalem church was made a year prior
Macedonian generosity was stirred by hearing of Corinthian zeal
Paul sent brethren ahead to ensure the gift was ready and preserve the church's witness
Generosity reflects the believer's heart and testimony for Christ

outline.title: Attitude Toward Generosity
subpoints: Sowing sparingly results in reaping sparingly
Giving should be according to one's purpose in the heart
God loves a cheerful giver, not one who gives grudgingly or under obligation

outline.title: Reward for Being Generous
subpoints: God makes all grace abound toward the giver
Believers are enriched in everything for all liberality
Generosity causes thanksgiving to God through the ministry

outline.title: Glory of God in Generosity
subpoints: The administration of the service supplies the needs of the saints
The proof of the ministry glorifies God for the obedience of the confession to the gospel

outline.title: The Gospel in Generosity
subpoints: Generosity is linked to the exceeding grace of God
The indescribable gift of God is the ultimate motivation and result

summary:
In this sermon, Pastor Tito Lyro explores the theme of the grace of giving through an exposition of 2 Corinthians 9. The message emphasizes that generosity is not merely a financial transaction but a critical component of a believer's testimony and witness for Christ. Paul’s repeated exhortation to the Corinthians highlights the importance of following through on promises, as their willingness to support the Jerusalem church had already inspired the Macedonians. The sermon underscores that a believer's actions regarding money, time, and skills reveal the state of their heart and their allegiance to God.

The teaching addresses the attitude required for true generosity, contrasting grudging obligation with the cheerful giving that God loves. It warns against the hypocrisy of appearing more generous than one actually is, citing the example of Ananias and Sapphira in Acts 5 to illustrate the seriousness of integrity in stewardship. The sermon further outlines the spiritual rewards of generosity, noting that God multiplies grace and resources to those who give liberally, resulting in thanksgiving and the glorification of God.

Ultimately, the message connects the act of giving to the broader narrative of the gospel. Generosity is presented as a response to the exceeding grace of God and a means by which the church demonstrates the reality of the gospel to the world. The sermon concludes by affirming that the administration of such service not only meets the needs of the saints but also serves as a powerful proof of the transformative power of Christ's grace.
